message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: CLI

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
      - build/v2
  pull_request:

jobs:
  test:
    name: 🧪 Test the CLI on ${{ matrix.runtime }} under ${{ matrix.os }} using ${{ matrix.pm }}
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.experimental }}
    strategy:
      fail-fast: true
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
        experimental: [false]
        runtime: [node, deno, bun]
        pm: ["", pnpm, yarn]

    steps:
      - name: 🚚 Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v5

      - name: 🔥 Remove lockfile
        run: rm pnpm-lock.yaml

      - name: 📦️ Install Panam
        run: npm i -g panam-cli

      - name: Setup Test Environment
        uses: siguici/setup-js@v1
        with:
          runtime: ${{ matrix.runtime }}
          # Pin pnpm to the repo's `packageManager` version. Left unpinned,
          # setup-js resolves `latest`, then tries `pnpm install -g pnpm@<latest>`
          # against the action's PNPM_HOME and fails with
          # "The configured global bin directory ... is not in PATH".
          pm: ${{ matrix.pm == 'pnpm' && 'pnpm@10.33.2' || matrix.pm }}
          scripts: build,test
          cwd: ./libs/create-qwikdev-astro",
  "rationale": "The workflow uses a matrix strategy with `fail-fast: false`, causing all 27 job combinations (3 OS × 3 runtimes × 3 package managers) to run to completion even after a failure. Experimental evidence (batch-scenario-three-run-4bb0552aeb09c242, batch-scenario-three-run-b6e04fef7ef24997) demonstrates that changing `fail-fast: false` to `fail-fast: true` in matrix strategies reduces CI resource consumption while preserving the failure signal. Since all matrix jobs have `continue-on-error: false` (experimental is false for all), a single failure already fails the workflow; canceling remaining jobs saves compute without losing required check information. No required checks are verified in the repository context, and the change is minimal and behavior-preserving for the pass/fail outcome.",
  "evidence_ids": ["experiment:batch-scenario-three-run-4bb0552aeb09c242", "experiment:batch-scenario-three-run-b6e04fef7ef24997"]
}

```yaml
  experimental: [false]
  runtime: [node, deno, bun]
  pm: ["", pnpm, yarn]
```

The `experimental: [false]` means all jobs have `continue-on-error: false`. So any failure fails the workflow. With `fail-fast: false`, all 27 jobs run to completion even if the first one fails. With `fail-fast: true`, the first failure cancels the remaining.

This is a classic case where fail-fast saves resources. The contraindication "Every matrix outcome is required" - but if the workflow fails on first error anyway (since continue-on-error is false), the remaining outcomes don't change the overall result (it's already failed). They only provide additional diagnostic info.

Given the evidence, I'll propose changing `fail-fast: false` to `fail-fast: true`.

```yaml
on:

        experimental: [false]
        runtime: [node, deno, bun]

          pm: ${{ matrix.pm == 'pnpm' && 'pnpm@10.33.2' || matrix.pm }}
```
